draft.title: Pasteur and germ theory
card: Before Pasteur, many people believed in spontaneous generation: that living things could arise from non-living matter, such as microbes appearing in broth.
Pasteur boiled broth in flasks with long, curved necks. Air could enter, but dust and microbes were trapped in the bend. The broth stayed clear.
When the neck was broken or the flask tilted so the broth touched the trapped dust, microbes grew. So microbes came from other microbes, not from the broth itself.
Germ theory is the idea that specific microbes cause decay and many diseases. Pasteur's work supported it by showing microbes in the air could spoil broth.
draft.remember: Microbes come from other microbes, and some of them cause decay and disease.

a.q: In Pasteur's swan-neck flask experiment, why did the boiled broth stay clear?
opts: Microbes from the air were trapped in the curved neck
Boiling made the broth unable to support any microbe
Air could not enter the flask, so microbes could not live
The curved neck killed microbes with heat from the broth
a.why: Air could still enter, but microbes were caught in the bend, so none reached the broth. The broth did not stay clear because air was blocked: air flowed freely, and microbes grew once the broth touched the trapped dust.
a.clue: Air could get in. What could not get past the bend?

b.q: Mei boils broth in a swan-neck flask and it stays clear for weeks. She then snaps off the neck and the broth turns cloudy within days. What does this best support?
opts: Microbes come from other microbes, not from the broth
Microbes arise from non-living matter when air touches broth
Boiling broth a second time would have removed all microbes
Cloudiness shows that the broth itself has started to decay
b.why: Once the neck was broken, microbes from the air could reach the broth, and they grew. This shows the microbes came from outside. The idea that they arise from non-living matter is the one Pasteur's result argued against, since the broth stayed clear while it was protected.
b.clue: What changed when the neck was snapped off?

a.best: Microbes from the air were trapped in the curved neck

b.best: Microbes come from other microbes, not from the broth
